quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal any time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently applying the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the steering wheel to force the vehicle back on.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions after you have started drinking.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and enter at the same speed as the traffic. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a roadway.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less when drinking beer instead of wine.
Less when drinking wine instead of beer.
More when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream affects you.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.
questions.explanation: When the driver behind you wants to pass, slow down to create space in front of your vehicle. This helps the other driver complete the pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train's horn. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection, at any stop line, and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. At high speeds, your tires may lose grip completely. The vehicle then slides on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you drive in a lane with a red X light?

options.text: If there is no visible oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Lane use control lights show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine may affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered crossing gates or the sound of a train.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcoholic drinks, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: A tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Steer straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and pull off the road at a safe spot.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need to push harder on the wheel. Slow down and drive to a safe spot off the road to stop.

questions.question: You see a steady green traffic light ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection go first. You can continue driving, but be ready to slow down or stop if the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign tells you that traffic only flows in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog when visibility is 500 feet or less. Do not use high beams—they reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours is like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagons (eight-sided). This shape is used only for stop signs to tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car with no one around. What should you do?

options.text: You must wait for the police.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, you must leave a written note that includes your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: When you must yield, you should also stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.
questions.correctAnswerText: True.
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot safely merge into the flow of traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Keep more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: When is it okay to text while driving?

options.text: At any time if the driver is under age 18.
At any time if the driver is age 18 or older.
If the driver can text without looking at their phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in emergencies.
questions.explanation: Do not text while driving, except in emergencies. Taking your eyes off the road increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move right to let them pass, if there is a right lane.
If you cannot move right, slow down gradually to encourage them to drive around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If tailgated, move right if possible. If not, slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but does not prevent impairment from drinking too much.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be prepared to stop safely before the intersection.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in your vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Look for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Look for other drivers in your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to cross ahead of them.
